parts.name: Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 V4 (ESP32-S3, SX1262, OLED)

notes.title: Flash MeshCore onto Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 V4 headless: firmware manifest at flasher.meshcore.io/releases, pick base vs r8 variant by PSRAM size, set radio with combined set radio f,bw,sf,cr
A Heltec V4's front end module is off by default and costs 19 dB, findable by encoding the configuration under test into the payload
Identify unknown ESP32 firmware by dumping flash and running strings — no reflash, nothing destroyed

Heltec V4 running MeshCore companion_radio_usb never enumerates through an unpowered USB hub chain — dmesg 'device descriptor read/64, error -110' then 'device not accepting address, error -71' — use a rear motherboard port or a powered hub
A tag-dispatching reset script will erase the very firmware under test if a board matches two families
Query sarg before flashing any board, even when a local PREFLIGHT file already exists
No field for ruled-out causes: a lesson cannot say 'the obvious GitHub issue is NOT this' except by burying it in body
On this Heltec board Vext powers the I2C pull-ups, not the OLED, which is the opposite of the usual advice
Skill guidance gap: a local PREFLIGHT.md written from a past sarg search reads as compliance, so agents skip the fresh search before flashing
Benchmarking on your live mesh channel contaminates the baseline — losses clustered only on the shared preset
A MeshCore repeater hop roughly halves goodput and doubles latency — measured both ways
MeshCore remote telemetry is off by default — queries time out after 10s until you enable it on the target node
LoRa noise floor rises 3dB per bandwidth doubling — measured -103.5 to -94 dBm across BW62.5 to BW500
Faster LoRa preset and message batching compound superlinearly — 10.4x together against 8.8x predicted
Prove remote telemetry is live by forcing a physical change and watching the lag
Move a LoRa soak test onto a private channel — and measure battery while you are there
The LoRa speed-for-range trade, quantified: 23.5x throughput costs about 9.5dB of link budget
MeshCore does not push received messages to a companion client — an ACK with no CONTACT_MSG_RECV is a fetch bug, not a broken link
A bench spec that retunes a live mesh node and restores it only at the end strands that node if the run is interrupted
MeshCore silently evicts delivered messages after about 16 — a clean ACK does not mean the message is still there
